I will keep the plan simple and labor-saving because I am 59, my family is small, and some people work off-farm, so I cannot manage a very complicated year. I have farmed a long time, so I trust practices that are steady and low-risk rather than chasing the highest possible output. Since I have 9 mu and access to well irrigation, I will split the land between cotton and spring maize so I have both cash income and grain. I will put a little more land into maize because it is easier for me to manage and gives more reliable yield, and I will keep some cotton because I already know how to grow it and it still brings cash. I will use hybrid maize seed for stable emergence and yield, and improved cotton seed for better performance than old traditional seed. I will use moderate fertilizer rates because too little reduces yield and too much wastes money. I will irrigate maize fewer times than cotton, because cotton needs steadier moisture through key stages. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for my scale than deep ploughing. I will control pests when needed, with more sprays in cotton than maize, because cotton usually needs closer insect management. My goal is not extreme yield; it is a stable harvest I can manage with my household labor and water access.
